entries.233ba1c34b12ff02: This business model purchases products from sports equipment manufacturers and other suppliers, sells them to general consumers through HIMARAYA stores nationwide and internet sales, and receives the sales proceeds.
entries.236f83a18ce84363: It sets its purpose as 'Designing Sports and Well-being,' classifies its business domains into 3 domains ('sports', 'lifestyle' and 'health'), and says it will work on building growth scenarios in each domain, centered on its operating know-how for physical stores and EC businesses and its capability to plan and develop original products. In Japan, it aims to expand sales channels through EC-exclusive sales and the development of new formats, and overseas through exports of its own-brand products and cross-border EC. For the fiscal year ending August 2026, the final year of the medium-term management plan, the company has revised its numerical plan because the business environment differs significantly from the premise assumptions, and positions the period as a phase for laying foundations aimed at rebuilding its earnings base; it says it will work on raising profitability of existing stores and expanding its EC business, centered on large-scale renovations of its main stores.

entries.e7007b76e7af470d: Its strength lies in its operations, which draw on the high expertise of a sports specialty retailer and reflect ideas developed bottom-up by in-house staff who have trusting relationships with customers in its products and services. The development of 'original brands' that are closely tied to everyday life and start from the customer's perspective, and the fulfillment system of consolidated subsidiary Koa Burein Co., Ltd., which handles everything from order receipt to shipment and customer support for internet sales, support both store and EC channels.
entries.f16818aa1b57d634: The business consists of a single segment, general retail business, and segment information is omitted. Revenue by product category for the fiscal year ended August 2025 was general sporting goods ¥38,064 million (63.0% of total), golf equipment ¥10,055 million (16.6%), outdoor equipment ¥8,177 million (13.5%) and ski and snowboard equipment ¥3,112 million (5.2%). There are 101 stores nationwide, mainly in western Japan: 10 stores in Gifu Prefecture (¥5,613 million), 10 in Aichi Prefecture (¥3,853 million), 9 in Yamaguchi Prefecture (¥3,411 million) and others. No customer accounts for 10% or more of revenue, and revenue from external customers outside Japan is at an immaterial level. In the competitive environment, direct sales by manufacturers through their own EC sites and market entry by companies from other industries, centered on apparel, are noted as prominent.
